habitat: Singly or in pairs in coastal and montane forest, mixed woodland, valley bush, riverine forest and suburban gardens.
summary: A common resident. A large, dull sunbird, olive-green, darker above and paler below. Sexes are alike. A rusty upper breast is often absent in the adult and usually present in the immature. An isolated eastern Zimbabwe population, sometimes treated as Western Olive Sunbird, lacks yellow pectoral tufts in the female. The call is a sharp tuk, tuk, tuk. The colour key is on the Olive page. The voice, pectoral tufts and rusty breast are printed on the Collared page, which names Western Olive Sunbird. No Kemp estimate is stored.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.

calls.description: A sharp tuk, tuk, tuk. The song is a reedy tsee-tsee-tsee-tsee, tseedlee, eedlee-id-id-id-seedle. This text is on the Collared Sunbird page. Grade A call from Everton Conservancy, Hillcrest, KwaZulu-Natal. The filename is XC1009162-Sunbird_Olive_EvertonConservancy_20250624_2_InterestingPrelude_NR10.mp3.
